correctness.rationale: Every coordinate on an n-cycle vanishes together or solves one finite-field power equation. The coefficient monomial includes a unit exponent, proving its uniform law; cyclic-group kernel size is gcd(2^ell−1,q−1), and disjoint cycles are independent. The permutation cycle index proves all moments exactly; Euler totient expansion proves the divisor-order second-moment product. Singularity analysis at roots of unity proves the fixed-q variance asymptotic, and negative covariance of distinct permutation cycle counts plus conditional independence gives Var(log I)=O_q(log n) and L² concentration. Exact brute-force multiplication independently checks every algebra over q=2,3,4 in n≤4 and q=5,7,8 in n≤3. No finite computation is used as proof of the infinite statements.

originality.rationale: Closest same-object older literature gives algebraic cycle decomposition over characteristic zero, not arithmetic random finite-field idempotent-count distributions. The recent finite-field source counts isomorphism classes of perfect evolution algebras and the newer whole-GL mean pertains to another sampling measure. An existing unweighted-cycle homomorphism count includes the same cyclic gcd factor and covers the all-unit-coefficient special case; this familiar arithmetic ingredient is not claimed as new. In contrast, the new claim proves the exact entire moment law, arithmetic variance asymptotics and a mean–typical gap for a specified random weighted monomial ensemble. Searches for aliases, higher/general coverage, table sequences and implication comparisons revealed no covering statement, although unlocated broader permutation-cycle-index refinements remain a genuine priority risk.

value.rationale: The number of idempotent elements solves the natural algebraic fixed-point equation x²=x. The discovery distinguishes uniformly sampled monomial perfect evolution algebras from all perfect evolution algebras, and obtains a previously unaccounted exact first-moment n+1 versus typical n^{κ_q} with κ_q<1. Prime-divisor orders of 2 determine nontrivial variance exponents, while the q=4 zero-only event has exact odd/even support and power decay. The full integer-moment law and concentration extend across all n and all finite fields, giving structural probabilistic information rather than an arbitrary finite census.
